correctness.rationale: Read complete fixed-tree RESULT.md and actual check.py tree entry. Han-Henk-Xue Proposition 2.1 supplies primitive normal projections; direct support-function evaluation gives D(z)=b(M-m)/2+|b(M+m)/2-sum a_i z_i|. Every integer normal of range>=2 has D>=b whereas every nonempty subset indicator has D=max(a(S),b-a(S))<b. Thus all minimizers must have range exactly one, so are ± indicators, proving the exact formula over unbounded integer normals. The construction a_i=2w_i, a_last=2W+1, b=6W+2 is polynomial in binary input and target b/2 iff original PARTITION holds; dynamic programming is pseudo-polynomial. Equal-coordinate optimum and centroid parity follow from ka=b/2. Independently checked three rational small instances by exhaustive primitive vectors in [-2,2]^n; finite box was not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for origin-translation dependence of the right-simplex first packing minimum and its exact lattice-normal rigidity and weak NP-completeness. Han-Henk-Xue 2026 Proposition 2.1 gives a general 1D lattice-projection identity and Theorem 1.3 calculates the centroid-centered simplex, but neither evaluates all positive barycentric translations nor establishes subset-sum hardness. The older difference-body minima are translation invariant. Resultary matching records did not show a broader translated-first-minimum solution.
residual_risks: A different differently named lattice-width/covering-normal formula might have the same subset discrepancy; unindexed literature not excluded.

final_claim: For K=b conv(0,e_1,...,e_n)-a, a_i>0, sum a_i<b, the origin-dependent first packing minimum is reciprocal to b/2+min_nonempty_S |sum_{i in S} a_i-b/2|, attained only by primitive normals ±1_S; binary-integer exact threshold is weakly NP-complete with n variable, and equal-coordinate translation maxima form ceil(n/2) positions.
limitations: All positive a_i with sum a_i<b, n>=2; for hardness even positive integer b and variable n; no other lattice or all simplices.
